assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential account of how technology and trade shocks reshape labour demand and wage inequality, with broad effects on empirical labour economics and public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the linked tasks, trade-shock and local-labour-market contribution.
assessment.maturity: The research programme has had ample time to shape subsequent work and policy-relevant empirical analysis.
uncertainties: The relative boundaries between technology, trade and institutional explanations of inequality remain contested.
Lawrence F. Katz is also important to the broader research programme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement and analysis of intergenerational mobility, making geographic and policy-relevant variation newly visible.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman provide a plausible three-person core for the central measurement and empirical research agenda.
assessment.maturity: The approach is established, widely applied and has generated a substantial subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The contribution combines data construction, measurement and interpretation, making the precise prize formulation important.
Lawrence F. Katz has relevant collaborative contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made transparent what data can and cannot establish under credible weak assumptions, an enduring contribution to empirical economic science.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure, while Tamer and Molinari provide a coherent connection to moment-inequality methods and inference.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and has diffused across applied and methodological econometrics.
uncertainties: The candidate combines several related methodological strands whose independent attribution requires careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of employer market power changed the baseline model used to understand wages, recruitment and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplies a central theoretical and empirical foundation; Naidu is a major contributor to the modern empirical expansion.
assessment.maturity: The programme has become central to labour economics and has clear policy relevance.
uncertainties: The breadth of the monopsony literature makes the appropriate set of laureates difficult to define.
The empirical magnitude and sources of employer power vary materially across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression supplied a foundational way to study heterogeneous conditional relationships rather than only averages.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the clear core for the original method; later distributional extensions should not obscure that attribution.
assessment.maturity: The method is deeply embedded in econometric theory and empirical practice.
uncertainties: Whether the methodological reach is sufficiently transformative for the prize relative to other econometric contributions is a judgment call.
Victor Chernozhukov's important later work is distinct from the foundational attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation has made long-run human-capital consequences empirically and conceptually central.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond anchor the early-life empirical evidence, while Cunha represents the connected dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated across settings and strongly influenced health and education economics.
uncertainties: The candidate spans empirical early-life shocks and structural theories of skill formation, which may be too broad for one citation.
Causal mechanisms and external validity differ across early-life interventions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical study of taxable-income responses gave modern optimal-tax analysis a more usable evidence base.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are central to linking taxable-income elasticities to tax design; Chetty contributed importantly to the broader empirical programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively absorbed into public-finance research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates depend on institutional setting, avoidance opportunities and the treatment of income shifting.
The creditable research programme is broad and overlaps with several adjacent public-finance traditions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods enabled credible empirical analysis where fixed effects, persistence and endogeneity otherwise create severe obstacles.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the indispensable core, with Blundell central to the subsequent system-GMM development.
assessment.maturity: These methods have been used widely for decades and remain standard tools in applied econometrics.
uncertainties: Practical performance can be sensitive to instrument proliferation and specification choices.
The method's widespread use does not by itself resolve concerns about misuse in applications.
